title: Hong Kong by Night
summary: Hong Kong as a city of Kuei-jin, Kin-jin and hengeyokai.

claims.text: For about 1500 years Hong Kong was a backwater ruled from Canton, its villages farming and fishing while Canton grew into a great trading city.
Its population has passed six million, and rents rise with the towers of the Central district.
Silent hunters move through the crowds after supernatural prey, and that prey is itself out hunting Chi to stay alive.
The harbour takes millions of tons of raw sewage each day, to the dismay of the hengeyokai.

title: Hong Kong Terms
summary: Local words used among the city's supernatural folk.

claims.text: Gweilo, ghost man, is a Chinese word for Westerners, once an insult and now a common label for non-Asians.
Hengeyokai are the shapeshifters of the East.
A hong is a major company, a godown a warehouse, and a hukou a permit fixing where someone must live.

title: Anguo Chun
summary: A Kuei-jin who seeks to rule the Cathayans of Hong Kong.

claims.text: Anguo Chun holds that the mortals of the city must be taught proper values in the old ways, with the care of fine calligraphy, and that Kuei-jin must stop following barbarian ways.
In this view any Kin-jin still in Hong Kong stays at its own peril.
Chun recently left Kowloon to live in the Central District.

title: Lantau Island
summary: The large outer island of Hong Kong.

claims.text: Lantau holds the Yin Hing Monastery, known for its Buddhist statues and paintings, and a Trappist house sworn to silence that lodges visitors.
Its main town, Tai O, is home to many Tanka boat people who have moved onto land.
